content: What's the difference between MLList and Std.Iterators.IterM? Should we deprecate MLList in favor of IterM?
I haven't used IterM yet, but deprecating MLList, if all uses of it can be replaced by IterM, seems reasonable to me.
Yes, no one should be using MLList anymore.

@Kim Morrison

I had been waiting for MLList to be deprecated, but it seems it hasn’t been deprecated yet.

I’d be happy to submit that PR. What do you think?

I'm not entirely convinced that docs#Std.Iterators.IterM can always be replaced by docs#MLList. First of all, docs#Std.Iterators.IterM is parameterized by the state type and thus you can't really pass it around as datastructure. Furthermore, the transformation operations on docs#Std.Iterators.IterM don't really do anything but return an iterator with a different state type. So one thing you cannot really do with IterM is to transform it in a loop (but that's also not its purpose): Instead you should use IterM if what you want is to take some data, iterate it and produce some result but it's not suitable as a datastructure.
If that's what you use MLList for, sure, these uses can be replaced. But if you intend to use it as a datastructure, I don't think IterM works as a replacement.

@Kim Morrison

Sorry for the slow reply.

I also have doubts about whether MLList can really be replaced by Std.IterM. I’m planning to try it out with some code I have locally that uses MLList.
I’ve confirmed that MLList can be replaced by IterM in my codebase. Ok!

@Kim Morrison

I've opened a PR: http://github.com/leanprover-community/batteries/pull/1887

The Nondet monad is implemented in terms of MLList. Should it be rewritten in terms of IterM, or should it also be deprecated, like MLList?
Right, you can't really rewrite Nondet in terms of IterM because IterM is not a functor or monad in the normal sense.
